records.name: Euphorbia roemeriana

morphology.leaves: Main foliage obovate/oblanceolate; flowering branch bracts opposite, semicircular, fused sometimes nearly halfway
morphology.inflorescence: Cyathium glands bear one erect horn at either end, no broad gland appendages

records.diagnostics: Opposite semicircular bracts substantially fused at bases versus free bracts of E. spathulata
holds: Exact FNA capsule/seed measurements still need side-by-side source review
Old Montague County specimen likely erroneous per flora; Williamson County reported, not BONAP county certification

records.name: Euphorbia serpens

morphology.habit: Annual; slender thread-like prostrate stems often rooting at nodes
morphology.leaves: Opposite small entire broadly ovate/round blades, existing FNA-based 2–7(–9) × 2–6 mm
morphology.stipules: Fused, broad triangular scales at nodes (FNA-based, 0.5–1.2 mm)
morphology.seed: FNA-based pale smooth seeds about 0.7–1.1 × 0.4–0.7 mm
morphology.habitat: Stream bottoms, prairies, clay flats, disturbed ground

records.diagnostics: Rooting nodes and broad fused stipules; unlike E. prostrata, mature fruit glabrous and seeds largely smooth
holds: FNA figures marked distinctly from printed 1999 account

records.name: Euphorbia simulans
records.historical: Chamaesyce simulans (L.C.Wheeler) Mayfield or Euphorbia polycarpa var. simulans L.C.Wheeler; absent from located 1999 flora

morphology.habit: Prostrate slender annual or short-lived perennial, 5–40 cm (FNA-based project profile)
morphology.leaves: Opposite round to short oblong 1–3.2 × 1.5–5 mm, glabrous, often relatively symmetric at base
morphology.cyathia: Usually solitary, four red-purple elliptic glands; appendages absent
morphology.seed: Repository FNA-based 1.5–2 mm, four-angled, weak transverse ridges; stronger distinction from E. theriaca by mature seed morphology
morphology.habitat: West Texas Trans-Pecos, Brewster, Hudspeth, Presidio counties cited in FNA

records.diagnostics: Tiny almost round leaves and purplish naked glands; FNA emphasizes mature seed comparison to E. theriaca
holds: Not documented for Hays range in verified reference; keep range provisional and exclude from native count until BONAP review
Full FNA key measurements not exhaustively compared with repo existing profile

records.name: Euphorbia spathulata
records.source: 1999 Flora genus key + account; FNA for secondary traits

morphology.leaves: Numerous oblanceolate blunt-tipped leaves, finely toothed at least toward apex
morphology.bracts: Floral bracts mostly wider than long, typically separate rather than fused
morphology.cyathia: Round unhorned involucral glands, without conspicuous appendages
morphology.fruit: Warty (verrucose) capsule, unlike smooth E. roemeriana
morphology.habitat: Detailed continuation after p.609 requires check

records.diagnostics: Fine marginal teeth plus warty capsules and unhorned glands vs fused-bract, smooth-fruited E. roemeriana
holds: 1999 species account continues beyond retrieved passage; don't fabricate flowering months or habitat
Modern FNA may differ in seed sculpture across geographical range

records.name: Euphorbia villifera

morphology.habit: Perennial, can flower as first-year annual; ascending/erect stems to 40 cm
morphology.leaves: 3–10 mm long, entire or very finely toothed; often triangular in 1999 key
morphology.indumentum: 1999 key conspicuous soft hairs 0.8–1.5 mm and broad thin leaves, though FNA-backed profile allows glabrous variants
morphology.cyathia: Styles forked about half to two-thirds their length
morphology.fruit: 1999 key: capsule 1.3–1.9(–2.1) mm; FNA-backed dimensions differ and should stay source-separated

records.diagnostics: Ascending hairy sandmat with small leaves and free threadlike stipules, versus prostrate E. serpens with fused scales
holds: Differences between the 1999 pubescence character and FNA glabrous forms require geographic reconciliation

records.name: Jatropha dioica
records.historical: Jatropha dioica Sessé ex Cerv. (no confirmed 1999 species passage in retrieved search)
records.source: Flora of North America and Texas A&M

morphology.habit: Perennial woody-based rubbery-stemmed shrub/subshrub 0.3–0.9 m (Texas A&M)
morphology.leaves: Usually narrow linear to oblanceolate; plants can be nearly leafless part of season
morphology.flowers: Small white or pinkish-white tubular flowers; FNA var. dioica staminate petals 5–6 × about 1.5 mm, 10 stamens in 2 whorls
morphology.roots: Perennial underground rootstocks/woody base; dimensions unverified
morphology.fruits: Three-lobed capsule (genus); quantitative treatment not yet extracted
morphology.habitat: Texas calcareous and rocky upland, specific county status pending

records.diagnostics: Rubbery branching stems and small white-to-pink flowers, with variable leaf width across varieties
holds: Old 1999 flora page not directly found; avoid assigning precise page
Var. dioica versus var. graminea require source-level assessment; no cultivar substitution

records.name: Ricinus communis

morphology.habit: Large monoecious annual in north central Texas, 1–5 m
morphology.leaves: Alternate peltate leaves, petiole to 30 cm, (5–)7–9(–11) deep palmately lobed segments with gland-tipped toothed margins
morphology.flowers: Terminal panicle/raceme; staminate flowers lower, pistillate upper; 5 sepals, no petals, numerous stamens, 3 red plumose styles
morphology.fruit: Round often softly spiny capsule 12–20 mm diameter
morphology.habitat: Cultivated and escaped around roads, fill, waste areas

records.diagnostics: Peltate deeply divided large leaves and spiny three-locular fruit; NOT a Hays County native
holds: Extremely toxic seeds; avoid handling and do not encourage ingestion
Native Africa/west Asia; excluded from local native counts

records.name: Stillingia texana

morphology.habit: Perennial stems decumbent to erect, up to 65 cm
morphology.leaves: Linear 2–5 mm wide (genus key), finely toothed
morphology.flowers: Terminal spikes with staminate above pistillate flowers (genus pattern)
morphology.fruit: Capsules ca. 6 mm long and wide; gynobase lobes 3–3.5 mm
morphology.habitat: Gravelly and rocky calcareous soils; Edwards Plateau

records.diagnostics: Narrow linear leaves 2–5 mm and 6-mm capsules vs broader leaves 9–30 mm and ~12-mm capsules of S. sylvatica
holds: BONAP local county mapping not verified
